quests.instruction: One of these words has a vowel sound unlike the others. Which one?
quests.hint: Listen to the vowels. Two of them sound the same.
quests.explanation: “Snow” and “coat” have long o. “Cloud” has /ow/.
quests.funFact: Snow and coat both have long o, but cloud uses ou to make a different sound, /ow/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a silent letter and a short vowel?
quests.hint: Look for a silent letter first. Then check the vowel sound.
quests.explanation: “Knit” has a silent k and short i. “Knee” has a silent k but a long e, and “kite” has no silent letter.

quests.instruction: Which number of syllables matches “crocodile”?
quests.hint: Clap the beats as you say it slowly.
quests.explanation: “Crocodile” has 3 syllables: croc-o-dile.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel sound as “shirt”?
quests.hint: Say shirt and listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Shirt” and “nurse” both have /er/. “North” has /or/ and “nail” has long a.
quests.funFact: Nurse, shirt and fern all have the same /er/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has a soft c and a long i?
quests.hint: You need both clues in one word.
quests.explanation: “Nice” has a soft c before e and a long i from the i_e pattern. “City” has a short i and “kite” has no c.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with a blend and has the /oy/ sound?
quests.hint: Look at both the beginning and the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Spoil” starts with sp and has oi for /oy/. “Spoon” has long oo and “spill” has short i.

quests.instruction: In which word does the y at the end say long e?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which one ends with a sound like the e in me?
quests.explanation: “Bunny” ends with y saying long e. “Sky” and “fly” are short words where y says long i.
quests.funFact: Bunny, baby, candy and happy all end with y saying long e.

quests.instruction: Which word is divided into syllables correctly?
quests.hint: Split the word where two consonants sit side by side.
quests.explanation: “Basket” divides bas-ket, with a closed first syllable.

quests.instruction: Only one of these words ends with /t/ instead of /d/ or /id/. Which one?
quests.hint: Which word finishes with a quick, quiet tap?
quests.explanation: “Kicked” ends with /t/. “Hugged” ends with /d/ and “painted” ends with /id/.

quests.instruction: Which of these pairs has a matching vowel sound?
quests.hint: Say both words in each pair.
quests.explanation: “Pie” and “high” both have long i, spelled ie and igh.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /r/ even though it starts with w?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the first sound.
quests.explanation: “Wrong” starts with /r/, and the w is silent. “Wing” and “wind” start with /w/.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /j/ sound in the middle?
quests.hint: Listen to the sound that follows the first syllable.
quests.explanation: “Magic” has a soft g that says /j/. In “magnet” and “mango”, the g says /g/.
quests.funFact: In “magic”, the g says /j/ because it comes before the letter i.

quests.instruction: Silent letters do not count. Which word has just three sounds?
quests.hint: Count only the sounds you can hear in each word.
quests.explanation: “Knight” has 3 sounds: /n/ /ī/ /t/. “Frost” has 5 and “chimp” has 4.
quests.funFact: Silent letters like the k and gh in knight are part of the spelling but not part of the sound.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT rhyme with “night”?
quests.hint: Say each word and listen to the ending.
quests.explanation: “Night”, “kite” and “light” rhyme. “Knit” has a short vowel.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the same sound as “bridge”?
quests.hint: Listen to the very last sound.
quests.explanation: “Bridge” and “judge” both end with /j/ spelled dge.

quests.instruction: Which word spells long a in a different way from the other two?
quests.hint: Look at the letters that spell the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Rain” and “wait” both use ai. “Cake” uses a_e.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with /sk/ but is NOT spelled with sk?
quests.hint: Look for the word that starts with sc.
quests.explanation: “Scarf” starts with /sk/ spelled sc, because c says /k/ before a. “Skip” spells it sk.
quests.funFact: Words like scarf and scout begin with /sk/ but are spelled with sc.

quests.instruction: Which word has two syllables and a long a in the first syllable?
quests.hint: Divide each word and check the first vowel.
quests.explanation: “Lazy” divides la-zy, with an open first syllable and long a. “Rabbit” and “happy” have short a.

quests.instruction: Which word has both a digraph and an r-controlled vowel?
quests.hint: You need two clues in one word.
quests.explanation: “Shark” has the digraph sh and /ar/. “Ship” has no r-controlled vowel and “star” has no digraph.

quests.instruction: Find the word where ou says /ow/.
quests.hint: Look for ou and listen for /ow/.
quests.explanation: “Mouth” has ou saying /ow/. “Moth” and “month” have short vowels.
quests.funFact: Mouth, house, cloud and round all use ou for the /ow/ sound.

quests.instruction: Where does “mitten” split into syllables?
quests.hint: Divide between the two matching consonants.
quests.explanation: “Mitten” divides mit-ten, between the two t letters.

quests.instruction: Which word has the short oo sound, as in “book”?
quests.hint: Think of the vowel in book. Which word has the same quick sound?
quests.explanation: “Foot” has the short oo sound. “Food” has long oo and “fort” has /or/.
quests.funFact: Foot, book, good, cook and wood all have the short oo sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /f/ sound spelled ph?
quests.hint: Look for ph in the middle of a word.
quests.explanation: “Elephant” has ph for /f/. “Elbow” and “envelope” have no /f/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has /er/ spelled ir?
quests.hint: Find the word with the letters ir.
quests.explanation: “Third” has ir saying /er/. “Thorn” has /or/ and “thumb” has short u.

quests.instruction: Find the mistake. Which word was not changed correctly when -ing was added?
quests.hint: Think about the vowel in run. Is it short or long?
quests.explanation: “Run” needs a doubled n before -ing: running.

quests.instruction: Which spelling is wrong?
quests.hint: Remember the spelling of long i in light and night.
quests.explanation: The word is spelled “bright”, with igh.
quests.funFact: Light, night, bright and fight all use igh for long i.

quests.instruction: Which spelling of the word for a loud sound is wrong?
quests.hint: Remember that oi usually comes before a consonant in the middle of words.
quests.explanation: “Noise” uses oi, not oy, because oy usually comes at the end of a word.

quests.instruction: Which word has the most sounds?
quests.hint: Count the sounds in each word. A digraph counts as one.
quests.explanation: “Splash” has 5 sounds: /s/ /p/ /l/ /a/ /sh/. “Shop” and “chat” each have 3.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /ch/ /ar/ /j/?
quests.hint: Check the last sound. It is /j/.
quests.explanation: “Charge” has /ch/ /ar/ /j/, with a soft g at the end. “Chart” ends with /t/ and “change” has long a.

quests.instruction: Which word has four syllables?
quests.hint: Clap each word and count.
quests.explanation: “Caterpillar” has 4 syllables: cat-er-pil-lar. “Dinosaur” and “umbrella” each have 3.
quests.funFact: Long words get easier when you clap them one chunk at a time.
